State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Lt. Gurnur Singh Mahiwal vs M/S Country Colonisers Pvt. Ltd. on 4 January, 2018
2nd Additional Bench

 STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION,
 PUNJAB, CHANDIGARH

 Consumer Complaint No. 3 of 2017

 Date of Institution : 03.01.2017
 Date of Reserve : 20.12.2017
 Date of Decision : 04.01.2018

1. Lt. Gurnur Singh Mahiwal son of Maj. Gen. Y.S. Mahiwal C/o
Mr. I.S. Bajwa, House No. M185, Sector 25, Noida (UP).

2. Maj. Gen. Y.S. Mahiwal son of Sh. Harvel Singh C/o Mr. I.S.
Bajwa, House No. M185, Sector 25, Noida (UP).
 ....Complainants

 Versus

1. M/s Country Colonisers Private Limited through its Director

having its registered office at P.O. Rayon and Silk Mills, Adjoining

Coca Cola Depot, G.T. Road, Chheharta, Amritsar, Punjab-

143105.

2. M/s Country Colonizers Private Limited through its Authorised

Signatory Site Office at Sector 85, District S.A.S. Nagar, Mohali,

Punjab 160062.

 ....Opposite Parties

3. Housing Development Finance Corporation Limited, SCO No.

153-154, Sector 8-C, Chandigarh.

 ....Proforma-OP

 Consumer Complaint under
Section 17
of
 the Consumer Protection Act, 1986.
 Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 2

Quorum:-

 Shri Gurcharan Singh Saran, Presiding Judicial Member.
 Shri Rajinder Kumar Goyal, Member

Present:-

 For the complainants : Sh. Deepak Aggarwal, Advocate

 For Op No. 1&2 : Sh. Tejeshwar Singh, Advocate

 For Op No.3 : Ms. Anjali Moudgil, Advocate for
 Sh. Shekhar Verma, Advocate

GURCHARAN SINGH SARAN, PRESIDING JUDICIAL MEMBER

 ORDER
Complainants have filed this complaint against the

opposite parties (hereinafter referred as Ops) under
Section 17
of

the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 (for short the Act) on the

averments that complainants had applied for the apartment with

Ops for basic sale price of the flat as Rs. 74,62,500/-. Out of which

a sum of Rs. 72,90,875/- stand already paid. It has been further

stated that the complainants purchased the flat in question from the

original allottees Mr. Varun Sharma and Mr. Vinay Sharma through

Op Nos. 1 & 2, therefore, they have come in the footsteps of

original allottees. The flat was purchased by them exclusively for

the purpose of their self living. Flat No. 403, Tower Erica, Floor 4th,

Type 3 BHK+S in Group Housing, namely, Wave Gardens, SAS

Nagar, Mohali was allotted to the complainants. The complainants

had opted subvention plan under which they were required to pay

as under:-
Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 3
Payment Plan

 Subvention Linked Plan

 On Booking 3.0 Lacs for 2 BHK,
 5.0 Lacs for 3BHK
 & 3+S BHK
 Within 45 days of booking 15% 15%
 of Sale Price less Booking
 Amount
 Excavation upto five feet 25%

 On completion of Fourth Floor 25% + 100% of PLC
 Roof Slab
 On completion of Super 25%
 Structure / Brick Work
 On completion of Internal + 100% of car
 Plastering parking
 On offer of Possession 10% + Other applicable
 charges + Stamp
 Duty & Registration
 charges
 100%

The additional charges were to the tune of Rs. 3,73,125/- i.e. car

parking usage Rs. 1,50,000/-, club membership Rs. 75,000/- and

interest free maintenance security Rs. 99,500/-. In that way, the

total sale price came to Rs. 81,60,125/-. The complainants

continued to visit the site but there was no development. The

complainants waited upto December, 2016 but Ops did not offer

the possession, therefore, alleging deficiency in service on the part

of Ops, this complaint has been filed by the complainants against

the Ops for refund of Rs. 72,90,875/- alongwith interest @ 13%

p.a., which comes to Rs. 15,37,260/-, compensation of Rs. 5 Lacs

and Rs. 1 Lac as litigation expenses.
2. Upon notice, Ops appeared and filed their respective

reply. Op Nos. 1 & 2 in their reply took the preliminary submissions
Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 4
that the complainants are not consumer as defined under
Section

2(1)(d)
of the Act as the unit in question was purchased for

commercial purposes; the complaint is not maintainable in view of

the Arbitration Clause i.e. Clause No. 13 of the Apartment Allottee

Arrangement; the complainants had opted for subvention plan

under which the complainants paid just 15% of the Basic Sale Price

and the remaining amount was paid by the Bank and tripartite

agreement was executed between the complainants, Ops and the

bank and for the period of 24 months pre-Emi interest was to be

paid by Ops and it was further extended by the end of December,

2014. The period of handing over possession was extended upto

30.6.2018. It has been further stated that the complainants failed to

adhere the payment plan. The Service Tax and excavation of 5

feet, payment was payable by 22.12.2012, as per the demand

notice dated 3.12.2012 but it was paid on 12.6.2013 and moreover,

Service Tax of Rs. 61,238/- was not paid and accordingly, another

notice dated 25.3.2014 was issued to send the payment by

15.4.2014. Thereafter upto 4th floor slab completion, the demand

included PLC amount of Rs. 3,73,125/- and Service Tax of Rs.

1,03,767/- vide demand notice dated 24.5.2014. A part payment

was made on 16.12.2014 vide two cheques i.e. of Rs. 2,37,000/-

and Rs. 2 Lacs. There was delay of 18 months in payment of

service tax and there was delay of 11 months in payment of PLC of

Rs. 3,73,125/- and Service Tax of Rs. 1,03,767/-. Further a sum of

Rs. 59,799.56p had become due on completion of super structure

and was to be paid by 10.9.2015 is still unpaid till date. Out of the
Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 5
total payment of Rs. 72,90,875/-, the complainants had paid only a

sum of Rs. 16,94,000/-. The Ops had paid huge payments on

behalf of the complainants in the form of pre-EMI interest equal to

Rs. 5,58,043/-, rather, Ops have a cause of action to recover this

amount from the complainants. According to Clause 5.5 of the

agreement, in case there is delay in delivery of possession beyond

36 months, the complainants are entitled to penalty @ Rs. 5/- per

sq. ft. per month. The complainants are themselves defaulters,

therefore, they are not entitled to the refund. Further there was

some critical area for which the land was to be acquired by the

State Government, which they did not acquire. In this regard,

Memorandum of Agreement (in short MOA) dated 3.2.2006 was

executed and request was made to the Land Acquisition Collector,

GMADA vide letter dated 19.1.2012 to acquire 23.21 acres of land,

which falls within the Master Plan of the project but the State

Government failed to initiate the acquisition proceedings and to

deliver the possession of that land to the Ops; intricate questions

are involved, which cannot be settled in the summary procedure,

therefore, the matter be referred to the Civil Court and that the

complaint does not fall within the pecuniary jurisdiction of this

Commission. In parawise reply, on facts the averments stated in

the preliminary submissions/objections were reiterated. It has been

stated that the possession could not be delivered due to non-

acquiring of critical area of 23.21 acres of land by the State

Government as per MOA dated 3.2.2006. It has also been

reiterated that the payments were made late. In case the
Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 6
complainants themselves are defaulters then they cannot seek for

the refund. There is no deficiency in service on the part of Ops.

Complaint is without merit, it be dismissed.
3. Op No. 3 in its written reply took the preliminary

objections that the complaint is directed only against Op Nos. 1 & 2

and not against Op No. 3. This Op has advanced the finance to the

complainants and tripartite agreement was executed between the

parties under which the complainants have availed a loan of Rs.

55,96,875/-, out of sanctioned loan amount of Rs. 59,70,000/- and

on 6.2.2017, the complainants have paid a sum of Rs. 7,34,225/-

towards EMIs and as on 31.1.2017, a sum of Rs. 54,75,859/- is

outstanding. There is no deficiency in service on the part of Ops.

Complaint is without merit, it be dismissed.
4. Parties were allowed to lead their respective evidence.
5. Complainants in their evidence have tendered affidavits

of complainants i.e. Lt. Gurnur Singh Mahiwal and Maj. Gen. Y.S.

Mahiwal as Exs. C-A and documents Exs. C-1 to C-8. On the other

hand, Op Nos. 1 & 2 have tendered affidavit of Raghav Sharma,

Auth. Signatory as Ex. Op-1/A and documents Ex. Op-1/1 to Op-

1/26. Op No. 3 had tendered affidavit dated 27.7.2017 Ex. Op-3/A

and documents Exs. Op-3/1 to 3/4.
6. We have heard the counsel for the parties and have

carefully gone through the pleadings of the parties, evidence and

documents on the record.
Miscellaneous Application No. 2134 of 2017
Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 7
7. Ops No. 1 & 2 have filed an application under
Section

89
of the CPC for referring the case for mediation by pleading that

in view of the order passed in "
Vikram Bakshi V. Sonia Khosla",

SLP NO.
6873 of 2010, the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that

Courts should emphasize the need of early resolution of the

disputes and resort to mediation provided under
Section 89
of the

CPC, therefore, the case be referred to the mediation. However,

we have gone through the application filed by the Ops and as also

pointed out by the counsel for the complainants that terms of

mediation have not been referred by the Ops in the application and

orally also counsel for the Ops was unable to tell the exact date

when the possession of the flat complete in all respects shall be

handed over to the complainants and what will be the fate of the

interest amount after the due date upto the date of delivery of

possession. Therefore, in the absence of any terms of resolution,

the matter cannot be referred to the mediation, otherwise, the case

is ready for arguments and has been fixed for arguments.

Therefore, at this stage, the application has been moved by the

Ops just to avoid the decision. We do not see any merit in the

application, the same is hereby declined.
Complaint on Merits
8. Preliminary objection has been taken by the Ops that

complicated questions of law and facts are involved, therefore, the

matter be referred to the Civil Court. In case we go through the

pleadings of the parties, the complainants had booked one

apartment with Ops Nos. 1 & 2 and had paid a sum of Rs.
Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 8
72,90,875/- as demanded by the Ops from time to time. Buyer's

agreement is there and Ops have failed to deliver the possession

within the time frame. It is only the interpretation of agreement and

then to see whether there is any deficiency in service on the part of

Ops. We do not see that any complicated questions of law and

facts are involved, which cannot be adjudicated by this

Commission. The benches of this Commission are headed by

retired High Court Judges/retired District & Session Judges, who

have long experience at their back and are fully competent to

decide such like matters.
In this regard, we are fortified by the

judgment of "
Dr. J.J. Merchant and others Vs. Shrinath

Chaturvedi
", 2002(6) SCC 635 wherein it was held that 'the State

Commission and District Forum are headed by retired High Court

Judges and officers of District Judge level and in our view, this is

not such a case which cannot be decided by the 'Consumer Fora'

after obtaining evidence and if need be after getting an expert

opinion'.
Further reference can be made to "
Shiv Kumar Agarwal

versus Arun Tandon and another
", 2007(2) CLT 287, decided by

the Hon'ble National Commission. In that case a plea that case

involves complicated questions of fact and law and will need expert

evidence, which is not possible in the summary proceedings

adopted by the Consumer Fora repelled - Consumer Forum which

is headed by Senior Judicial Officers, are capable of dealing with

even complex questions. Therefore, we are of the opinion that this

Commission is fully competent to decide this complaint and no

cause of action is made out to refer the case to the Civil Court.
Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 9
9. Ops No. 1 & 2 raised the objection that there is

arbitration clause No. 13 exists in the agreement and in case of any

dispute arose between the parties, the matter is to be referred to

the Arbitrator. The Ops have moved an application No. 473 of 2017

for referring the matter to Arbitrator, which was dismissed by this

Commission vide order dated 19.4.2017 by holding that under
Section 3
of the CP Act, additional remedy has been provided,

therefore, we are of the opinion that the Consumer Fora are duly

competent to deal with the complaint despite having the arbitration

clause in the agreement.
10. As per averments in the complaint, originally, the

Apartment No. 403, Tower Erica, 4th Floor, Type 3 BHK + S in

Group Housing Development Scheme named as "Wave Gardens",

was allotted to Mr. Varun Sharma and Mr. Vinay Sharma. As is

clear in the pleadings this unit was purchased by the complainants

from Varun Sharma and Vinay Sharma. In this regard, there is sale

agreement Ex. C-1 and receipts of payments dated 14.5.2012 vide

which a sum of Rs. 5 Lacs was paid to the Ops and receipt dated

19.9.2012 vide which a sum of Rs. 1 Lac was paid to the Ops,

receipt dated 27.9.2012 vide which a sum of Rs. 5,50,000/- was

paid to the Ops. It was transferred with the intervention of Ops No.

1 & 2 and then there is Apartment Allottees Arrangement dated

28.5.2013 executed between the Ops and the complainants.

According to Annexure-II, there was subvention plan, which has

been
referred above
in facts of the complaint. Annexure-I is the

payment/price details, which reads as under:-
Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 10
Apartment No. 403 Tower Name Erica Floor 4th Floor
Type : 3 BHK + S Area : 1990 Sq. Ft.
Particulars Details Amount (Rs.)
A) Basic Sale Price (BSP) @ Rs. 3750/- Sq. ft. 7462500
B) Additional Charges
1. Preferential Location Charges
(if any)
a) 5% on BSP @ Rs. 187.5/- Sq. 373125
 ft.
2. Car Parking Usage Rights
a) Covered Rs. 150000/- 150000
b) Open R. N/S/-
2. Club Membership Charges Rs. 75000/- 75000
3. Interest Free Maintenance @ Rs. 50/- Sq. ft. 99500
Security (IFMS)
C) Down Payment Rebate
(10% on 95% of BSP minus
Booking Amount) @ Rs. N/S/- - -
Note : Down payment will have
to be made within 45 days of
allotment. Time is the essence.
Total (A + B) - C 8160125
Payment Plan Option Down Payment Subvention
 Plan Linked Plan
In this way, the total sale price of the apartment including PLC and

car parking charges and club membership comes to Rs.

81,60,125/- and out of that 10% was to be given at the time of

possession, which comes to Rs. 8,16,012.50p. As per the

statement of account issued by Ops on 13.12.2016 Ex. C-8, total

amount due including Service Tax is Rs. 73,50,674/- and total

receipt till date is Rs. 72,90,875/-, therefore, difference of just a

sum of Rs. 59,799/-. With regard to Service Tax, it is not necessary
Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 11
that it will be demanded in installments. Service Tax could be paid

at the end when actual delivery of the goods/apartment is offered

by the Ops. In this way, the payments as required upto date has

been made by the complainants. According to Clause 5.1 of the

agreement, the possession was to be delivered within a period of

30 months with extension period of six months and the date of

agreement is 28.5.2013. In this way, the Ops were required to

deliver the possession by 28.5.2016. Another fact is required to be

noted that payment was under subvention plan, which was allowed

by the Ops with Op No. 3. In this regard, there is a letter Ex. Op-1/3

dated 20.12.2014 vide which extension of subvention of Wave

Garden was allowed by the Ops. For this purpose, tripartite home

loan agreement was executed vide agreement Ex. Op-3/2. Loan

account No. 608403239 duly signed on behalf of Op Nos. 1 & 2

vide which a loan of Rs. 60 Lacs was sanctioned in favour of the

complainants and loan of Rs. 55,96,875/- was disbursed to the

complainants and paid to Op Nos. 1 & 2 on behalf of the

complainants. This period of subvention scheme was further

extended by Op Nos. 1 & 2 vide their letter dated 20.12.2014 Ex.
Op-1/3 vide which subvention scheme applicable to the

complainants was extended upto 31.12.2015 and then lateron it

was extended to 30.6.2018 vide their letter dated 4.8.2016 Ex. C-6.

Vide their email dated 5.3.2016, it has been mentioned by the Ops

that they will endeavour to deliver the possession by the end of

November, 2017. Counsel for the Ops was unable to say whether

the apartment/flat is complete and fit for delivery of the possession.
Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 12
Therefore, what is the legal position in case Ops failed to deliver

the possession within the promised time, it amounts to deficiency in

service and complainants can opt for refund. In this regard, a

reference can be made to the judgment of the Hon'ble National

Commission reported as II (2014) CPJ 131 "PUDA versus

Kanwalpreet Singh" that in case there is delay in handing over the

possession, it amounts to deficiency in service and refund order

can be passed. A reference has also been made to I (2017) CPJ

513 (NC) "Neha Suri versus Unitech Reliable Project Pvt. Ltd." In

that case, the possession of the flat was not given as agreed. It

amounts to deficiency in service. Amount deposited alongwith

interest was ordered to be refunded.
11. Counsel for the Ops was unable to rebut it that it is not

a deficiency in service on the part of Ops when they failed to

deliver the possession within the agreed time despite taking 90% of

the payment from the complainants. In that eventuality, the

complainants have a right to withdraw from the scheme.
12. Another point has been raised by the counsel for the

Op Nos. 1 & 2 that there is delay in making the payment by the

complainants. With regard to the installment, excavation upto 5 Ft,

the payment was to be made by 22.12.2012 on the basis of

demand notice dated 3.12.2012 Ex. Op-1/7, the amount was paid

on 12.6.2013. Another notice of payment was issued on 31.3.2014

to make the payment by 15.4.2014 and payment was made on

20.5.2014. Another notice was issued on 2.7.2014 asking the

payment by 25.7.2014 whereas a part payment was made on
Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 13
16.12.2014 vide cheque of Rs. 2,37,000/- and service tax of Rs.

61,328/- was paid with a delayed payment of 18 months. Service

Tax of Rs. 1,03,767/- was paid with the delay of 11 months and

PLC of Rs. 3,72,125/- with a delay of 11 months. With regard to the

Service Tax, we have already observed that Service Tax was not

agreed to be paid in installment. The Service Tax is liable to be

paid as and when the project is complete and it can be paid in

lumpsum. With regard to PLC and some other payments, there is

some delay in making the payment and according to the

agreement, in case there is delay in making the payments then the

complainants are liable to pay alongwith interest @ 18% p.a. In

case it is accepted being a clause in the agreement but in that

eventuality in case the Ops have failed to deliver the possession

within time and the complainants have withdrawn from the scheme

and complainants had asked for the refund then after paying the

penalty the payment of the complainants will be considered on the

original date and not on the date of payment and in return the Ops

will have to pay the similar rate of interest in case of refund.

Therefore, in case of refund penal interest cannot be allowed

because the complainants will be entitled to interest from the date

of payment and not from the date fixed for payment.
13. It has been further argued by the counsel for the Ops

that according to Clause No. 5.5, in case there is delay in delivery

of the possession then the Ops are liable to pay the penalty as per

Clause 5.5 i.e. @ Rs. 5/- per sq. ft. per month of super area from

the date, the possession was to be delivered upto the date of
Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 14
payment. Whereas it has been contended by the counsel for the

complainants that in case of late payment, the Ops are claiming

interest @ 18% then similar treatment be given to the

complainants. Complainants were at disadvantageous stage

because the flat/apartment was already allotted to Mr. Varun

Sharma and Mr. Vinay Sharma and others and it was purchased by

the complainants. It is one sided agreement and on account that in

case of default on the part of complainants, he has to pay 18%

interest whereas Ops are to pay just 3%. This question has been

dealt in detail by the Hon'ble National Commission in CC No. 427

of 2014 "Satish Kumar Pandey & Anr. Vs. M/s Unitech Ltd."

decided on 8.6.2015 wherein the Hon'ble National Commission

observed as under:-
"However, a term of a contract, in my view will not be final and

 binding if it is shown that the consent to the said term was not

 really voluntary but was given under a sort of compulsion on

 account of the person giving consent being left with no other

 choice or if the said term amounts to an unfair trade practice. It

 was submitted by the learned counsel for the complainants that

 the term providing for payment of a nominal compensation such

 as Rs.5/- per square foot of the super area having become the

 order of the day in the contracts designed by big builders, a

 person seeking to buy an apartment is left with no option but to

 sign on the dotted lines since the rejection of such term by him

 would mean cancellation of the allotment. He further submitted

 that a person seeking to acquire a built up flat instead of
Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 15
purchasing a plot and then raising construction on it, therefore, is

 not in a position to protest resist the inclusion of such a term in the

 Buyer's Agreement, and has to rely upon the reputation of the

 builder, particularly if he is a big builder such as Unitech Ltd. He

 also submitted that the format of the Buyer's Agreement is never

 shown to the purchasers at the time of booking the apartment and

 if he refuses to sign the Buyer's Agreement on the format provided

 by the builder, not only will he lose the booking, even the booking

 amount/earnest money paid by him will be forfeited by the builder.

 I find merit in the above referred submissions of the learned

 counsel. A person who, for one reason or the other, either cannot

 or does not want to buy a plot and raise construction of his own,

 has to necessarily go in for purchase of the built up flat. It is only

 natural and logical for him to look for an apartment in a project

 being developed by a big builder such as the opposite party in

 these complaints. Since the contracts of all the big builders

 contain a term for payment of a specified sum as compensation in

 the event of default on the part of the builder in handing over

 possession of the flat to the buyer and the flat compensation

 offered by all big builders is almost a nominal compensation being

 less than 25% of the estimated cost of construction per month, the

 flat buyer is left with no option but to sign the Buyer's Agreement

 in the format provided by the builder. No sensible person will

 volunteer to accept compensation constituting about 2-3% of his

 investment in case of delay on the part of the contractor, when he

 is made to pay 18% compound interest if there is delay on his part

 in making payment.
Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 16
It can hardly be disputed that a term of this nature is wholly one

 sided, unfair and unreasonable. The builder charges compound

 interest @ 18% per annum in the event of the delay on the part of

 the buyer in making payment to him but seeks to pay less than 3%

 per annum of the capital investment, in case he does not honour

 his part of the contract by defaulting in giving timely possession of

 the flat to the buyer. Such a term in the Buyer's Agreement also

 encourages the builder to divert the funds collected by him for one

 project, to another project being undertaken by him. He thus, is

 able to finance a new project at the cost of the buyers of the

 existing project and that too at a very low cost of finance. If the

 builder is to take loan from Banks or Financial Institutions, it will

 have to pay the interest which the Banks and Financial Institutions

 charge on term loan or cash credit facilities etc. The interest

 being charged by the Banks and Financial Institutions for financing

 projects of the builders is many times more than the nominal

 compensation which the builder would pay to the flat buyers in the

 form of flat compensation. In fact, the opposite party has not even

 claimed that the entire amount recovered by it from the flat buyers

 was spent on this very project. This gives credence to the

 allegation of the complainants that their money has been used

 elsewhere. Such a practice, in my view, constitutes unfair trade

 practice within the meaning of
Section 2(r)
of the Consumer

 Protection Act, 1986 since it adopts unfair methods or practice for

 the purpose of selling the product of the builder. Though, such a

 practice does not specifically fall under any of the Clauses of
Section 2(r) (1)
of the Act that would be immaterial considering

 that the unfair trades, methods and practices enumerated in
Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 17
Section 2(r) (1)
of the Act are inclusive and not exhaustive, as

 would be evident from the use of word "including" before the

 words "any of the following practices".
The same view was upheld by the Hon'ble National Commission in
CC No. 347 of 2014, "Swarn Talwar & Ors. Vs. Unitech Ltd.
"

decided on 14.8.2015.
A reference has also been made to the

judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in "K.A. Nagmani Vs.

Housing Commissioner, Karnataka Housing Board", C.A. No.

6730-6731, decided on 19.9.2012.
In that case, the District Forum

has allowed interest @ 12% p.a. and its appeal was dismissed by

the State Commission as well as the Hon'ble National Commission

and after relying upon the judgment of "
Ghaziabad Development

Authority Vs. Balbir Singh
", (2004) 5 SCC 65, the interest @

18% per annum on the deposited amount was allowed alongwith

Rs. 50,000/- as compensation.
Against the judgment of the Hon'ble

National Commission in "
Swarn Talwar & Ors. Vs. Unitech Ltd.",

C.C. No.
347 of 2014 (supra), Op preferred the appeal before the

Hon'ble Supreme Court i.e. Civil Appeal No. 35562 of 2015,

decided on 11.12.2015 and passed the order as under:-
"We have heard learned counsel for the appellant and

 perused the record. We do not see any cogent reason to

 entertain the appeal. The judgment does not warrant any

 interference.
The Civil Appeal is dismissed."
Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 18
14. However, it was further observed by the Hon'ble

National Commission in another judgment 2017(3) CLT 520 (NC)

"Ankur Goswami versus Supertech and another" wherein the

Hon'ble National Commission observed that this clause in the

allotment letter would be applied to the case where allottee is

seeking possession of the flat and where allottee is not seeking

refund of the amount. However, in the present case, the allottee is

seeking the refund, therefore, the penalty @ Rs. 5/- per sq. ft. will

not be applicable. Further under Rule 17 i.e. Rate of Interest on

refund of advance money upon cancellation of agreement of

Punjab Apartment and Property Regulation Rules, 1995, it has

been provided as under:-
"17. Rate of Interest on refund of advance money upon

 cancellation of agreement. - The promoter shall refund full

 amount collected from the prospective buyers under sub-

 section (1) of
section 6
together with interest thereon at the

 rate of twelve per cent per annum payable from the date of

 receipt of amount so collected till the date of re-payment."
In the above rule it has been observed to refund the amount

alongwith interest @ 12% p.a. The complainants have taken a loan

from Op No. 3 and the interest rate varied from 11% to 9%.

Therefore, to be just and reasonable, the complainants will be

entitled to interest @ 12% on the deposited amount.
15. In nutshell, the Ops have failed to deliver the

possession to the complainants as promised even after receiving
Consumer Complaint No. 03 of 2017 19
90% of the payment from the complainants, in this way, the Ops

are deficient in their services. Accordingly, we allow the complaint

and direct the Ops No. 1 & 2 as under:-
(i) refund a sum of Rs. 72,90,875/- alongwith interest

 @ 12% p.a. from the various dates of deposit till actual

 payment, minus interest already paid by Op Nos. 1 & 2

 to Op No. 3;
(ii) Op No. 3 will have the first charge whatever

 amount has been received by Op Nos. 1 & 2 from Op

 No. 3. Firstly Op Nos. 1 & 2 will make the payment to

 Op No. 3 of the amount due in their accounts against

 the complainants and the balance payment will be

 made to the complainants.
(iii) pay Rs. 1 Lac as compensation to the

 complainants in equal share; and

 (iv) pay Rs. 21,000/- as litigation expenses.
The above directions be complied by Ops No. 1 & 2
within a period of 45 days from the date of receiving of the copy of

the order, failing which the complainants shall be at liberty to

execute the order by filing application under
Sections 25
